item.research_question: How does ultrafine-grain microstructure affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?
item.processing_route: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 400 and 1800 rpm for 5 min
item.test_conditions: Oxidation at 850-1050 °C for 100 h in laboratory air
key_findings: Ultrafine-grain microstructure reduces oxidation kinetics by 12-48%
Parabolic rate constant is lower for ultrafine-grained samples
Activation energy for oxidation is higher for ultrafine-grained samples
Protective oxide scales of Al2O3 and Cr2O3 form on ultrafine-grained samples
Internal oxidation zone (IOZ) forms in ultrafine-grained samples
item.mechanism: The enhanced oxidation resistance of ultrafine-grained samples is attributed to the formation of a dense protective Cr2O3 layer followed by internal Al-rich oxide layered structure, which acts as a barrier for the oxidation process
quotes: The ultrafine-grained samples showed a phase transition from BCC/B2 to FCC structure

The presence of more GBs favoring outward flux of elements to form a dense chromia layer followed by internal Al-rich oxide layered structure is responsible for the enhanced oxidation resistance of the processed samples
The formation of the dense protective Cr2O3 layer followed by Al2O3 inner oxide layered structure in the processed samples is favored by ultrafine-grain microstructure
